defects: Default birth-context merge converted now through datetime before validating the numeric receipt. Rounding down could discard a valid equal receipt; rounding up could accept a strictly future receipt. Explicit numeric legacy birth comparison also used the rounded datetime limit.

PumpPortal creation-reference receipt was encoded from UTC discovery metadata, then checked against numeric seconds. An immediate common-entry consumer could discard the reference when the UTC observation led that numeric clock, leaving missing_age and no RPC request.
HotQueue admission used UTC-encoded seconds for reference/birth validation. Moving the parser receipt to actual numeric seconds exposed the inverse rounding case at queue admission.

repair.birth_merge: Use one actual numeric default clock and preserve numeric-seconds precision for comparison and receipt validation. Supported explicit datetime/unit encodings retain their parser semantics. No epsilon, ceiling, clamp, fabricated age or rewritten receipt.
repair.discovery: Capture the original numeric local parser receipt before UTC metadata; retain it in the untrusted creation reference. Discovery/event UTC fields remain separate, and neither source certifies mint birth or buy permission.
repair.queue: Use actual numeric seconds for native queue admission; all other HotQueue methods, ranking, waiting order, dedup, limits and expiry logic are unchanged.
repair.test_contract: One legacy parser test incorrectly equated a numeric receipt with separately observed UTC metadata. Replace that equality with exact checks against each deliberately distinct original clock. All its other birth/identity checks and every other existing reference test function are retained.
